Is industry dominance unique to one country?

Our evidence: For 2023–2025, the industry-only share is similar in the two curated national samples: 75.8% for the US and 76.4% for China. Adding collaborations changes the comparison, showing that the definition of industry participation matters.

Research context: Jurowetzki and colleagues study the movement of AI researchers into private-sector laboratories. Widder and colleagues discuss the resources and infrastructure that can favour large commercial developers. Our model-attribution percentages offer a separate, narrower view of this broader industry influence.

Jurowetzki et al. (2025) · AI & SocietyWidder et al. (2024) · Nature

Participation is not dominance.

The original dataset selectively tracks notable AI models. Category shares should not be read as overall national AI capability, nor should the unequal-length time periods be mistaken for continuous annual trends.

How this comparison was built

Source: Epoch AI · Notable AI Models (snapshot 20 Oct 2026).

Country attribution: Whole counting, including joint US–China models once per country.

Classification: Industry, Academia, Collaboration, Other, Unknown. Other and Unknown are grouped only for visual display. Ambiguous records remain flagged rather than reclassified arbitrarily.

Two definitions: industry-only vs Industry plus Collaboration, without changing the denominator.
